newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ - Analysts see USDA estimate 215-225 mln boxes.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ - Analysts see USDA estimate 215-225 mln boxes.

text.p: A larger and more mature tree population is likely to boost the Florida citrus crop from last season, industry sources said.

Sources put the U.S. Department of Agriculture's first estimate for the 1996/97 Florida crop between 215.0 million and 225.0 million 90-lb boxes. Last season's crop totaled 203.2 million boxes yielding 1.52 gallons per box.
The USDA will release its key report Friday at 0830 EDT.

"The fact that there are more bearing trees suggests that we should have more fruit," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "Even if yields are as low as last year there would be more per tree, because the trees are older."
Ganes put the estimate between 220 million and 225 million boxes.
"The crop is in excellent condition," said Bernard Savaiko, an analyst with Paine Webber, noting favorable crop reports from the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service.
He said the market has already absorbed an estimate between 220.0 million and 225.0 million boxes, and pegged the crop at 219.0 million boxes.
"Unless something drastic happens, like a frost, prices tend to move with the report for most of the season," he said.

Dean Witter analyst Celeste Georgakis was less optimistic about production this season. "I feel the crop might not be as large as people anticipated," she said, putting the estimate at only 215.0 million boxes.
"The crop is very scattered," she said. "You can go from grove to grove and see a different situation."

Georgakis said the market is not likely to respond to a forecast between 215.0 million to 220.0 million boxes, but could trade lower if the estimate exceeds 220.0 million boxes and rally if the estimate falls below 210.0 million boxes.
"The general consensus it the estimate will be close to Elizabeth's (Steger)," Georgakis said in reference to the closely-watched forecast by a private consultant, released in August.
That estimate put the crop at 215.0 million boxes.
